day_description: After breakfast at our hotel, we will visit St. Joseph’s Cathedral, the see of the Archdiocese of Hanoi and the oldest standing church—it was one of the first structures built by the colonial government of French Indochina and is modeled on Notre Dame de Paris. Next, we will visit the Ho Chi Minh Complex which includes his Mausoleum and stilt. This is where the leader lived and worked from 1954 until the last years of his life. Here, you will have the opportunity to learn about his simple way of life. You’ll also visit One Pillar Pagoda, one of the four iconic symbols of Hanoi. For lunch, you will experience a bowl of Pho (noodle soup with beef or chicken) and enjoy a cup of Egg Coffee. Afterwards, we will transfer to Bac Ninh Province. On arrival, visit Ngam Gao Parish Church, which is connected with the life of Servant of God Marcel Nguyễn Tân Văn, CSsR, a Vietnamese Redemptorist brother known for his simple faith, love for Jesus, and spiritual writings. Many Catholics admire him for his holiness and consider him an example of trust, humility, and childlike love for God. Afterward, we will return to Hanoi for dinner and overnight.

day_label: Day 4: Hanoi – Nam Định – Ninh Binh
day_description: After breakfast at our hotel, we will depart for Nam Dinh, a region well known for its strong Catholic heritage. Our first stop will be the Basilica of Immaculate Conception in Phú Nhai, one of the largest and most important Catholic churches in Vietnam, admired for its grand Gothic architecture and historical significance. Next, we will visit Kien Lao Church, an important pilgrimage site for Vietnamese Catholics, known for its peaceful atmosphere and deep spiritual devotions. After lunch, the journey continues to Ninh Binh, where pilgrims visit the remarkable Phát Diệm Cathedral. Built mainly of stone and wood, this unique cathedral blends traditional Vietnamese architectural elements with Catholic design, making it one of the most distinctive churches in Vietnam. We will have dinner at a local restaurant before returning for overnight at your hotel.

Inside, colorful lights illuminate the rock formations, creating a magical and mysterious atmosphere. In the evening, we will return to Hanoi for dinner at a local restaurant before overnight in your hotel.

In the afternoon, we will travel to La Vang, believed to be the site of a Marian Apparition in 1798, during the persecution of Catholics by the Emperor of Vietnam. We will visit the Basilica of Our Lady of La Vang, both ruins of the original (destroyed in the Vietnam War) and the current, new Basilica. We will conduct a Rosary walk at the site. Afterward, we will return to Hue for dinner at a local restaurant before overnight in your hotel.

day_label: Day 7: Huế – Hội An - Our Lady of Trà Kiệu Shrine – Hội An
day_title: Huế – Hội An - Our Lady of Trà Kiệu Shrine – Hội An
day_description: After breakfast at our hotel, we will visit Immaculate Heart of Mary Cathedral (also known as Phủ Cam Cathedral), one of the largest, famous and oldest churches in Hue. Next, we will visit the Imperial Citadel – first built by King Gia Long in 1805. Here you will visit Ngo Mon Gate, Thai Hoa Palace, The Mieu Temple, and the Nine Dynastic Urns. After lunch at a local restaurant, we will transfer to Hoi An. Upon arrival, visit the Shrine of Our Lady of Trà Kiệu, one of the most important Marian pilgrimage sites in Vietnam. Located in the historic Catholic village of Trà Kiệu, the shrine commemorates the Trà Kiệu Marian Apparition, when local Catholics believed that Mary appeared and helped protect them during a time of persecution. Today, pilgrims come here to pray, attend Mass, and honor Mary, seeking her intercession and experiencing a deep sense of peace and faith. We will then have dinner at a local restaurant, followed by free time to explore Hội An Ancient Town by night.
activities: Visit Immaculate Heart of Mary Cathedral (Phủ Cam Cathedral); Visit Imperial Citadel (Ngo Mon Gate, Thai Hoa Palace, The Mieu Temple, Nine Dynastic Urns); Lunch; Transfer to Hoi An; Visit Shrine of Our Lady of Trà Kiệu; Dinner; Free time to explore Hội An Ancient Town by night

day_title: Hoi An – Đà Nẵng – Flight to Ho Chi Minh City
day_description: After breakfast at our hotel, we will transfer to Da Nang Airport for our flight to Ho Chi Minh City. We will then visit the Church of the Sacred Heart of Jesus (Tân Định Church) in Danang if time permits. Upon arrival in Ho Chi Minh City, we will have lunch at a local restaurant. After lunch, we will visit St. Philip the Apostle Church (Huyen Sy Church), one of the oldest and most beautiful Catholic churches in the city. Built in the early 20th century by the wealthy Catholic benefactor Philippe Le Phat Dat (Huyen Sy), the church features elegant Gothic architecture and remains an important place of worship for local Catholics. Next, we will continue to the Cathedral Basilica of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception, a famous landmark built during the French colonial period. Known for its red-brick façade and twin bell towers, the cathedral is one of the most iconic Catholic churches in Vietnam and a symbol of the city’s history and faith. Finally, we will visit the Independence Palace (also known as Reunification Palace), an important historical site where the Fall of Saigon took place. The palace offers visitors a glimpse into Vietnam’s modern history and the events that led to the reunification of the country. We will have dinner at a local restaurant before overnight at our hotel.

day_description: After breakfast, we will depart from Ho Chi Minh City for Vung Tau, a coastal city known for its beautiful beaches and important Catholic pilgrimage sites. The first stop is the Shrine of Our Lady of Bai Dau. Located on a peaceful hillside facing the sea, this shrine is a beloved place of prayer where pilgrims come to honor Mary and seek her intercession. Next, we will visit the famous Christ the King of Vũng Tàu, one of the largest statues of Jesus Christ in Asia. Standing on Mount Nhỏ, the statue overlooks the sea and the city, offering visitors a panoramic view after climbing the steps to the top. Afterward, we will return to Ho Chi Minh City for dinner at a local restaurant followed by overnight at your hotel.

day_description: After breakfast, we will visit the Church of Our Lady of Perpetual Help (Ky Dong Church), an important Catholic church located in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City. The church is well known as the headquarters of the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer (Redemptorists) in Vietnam. Afterward, we will travel to Vinh Long. After lunch, we will visit the Vietnam Martyrs’ Pilgrimage Center in Thanh Đức Commune, followed by a trip to Đình Khao where St. Philípphê Phan Văn Minh was martyred, before continuing to St. Philípphê Phan Văn Minh Church (Dinh Khao Church). Afterward, we will travel to Can Tho for dinner at a local restaurant followed by overnight at our hotel.

In the afternoon, we will head back to Cần Thơ for dinner at a local restaurant and overnight in our hotel.
